records.name: United Street Art
records.summary: A nonprofit formed in 2022 to support street artists and graffiti writers. It runs STEP OUTSIDE, a live street art exhibition program, publishes Priority Mag and Sticker Movie the Zine, and holds a monthly drawing meetup called Return to Sender.
records.what_you_do: Go to a STEP OUTSIDE exhibition, where graffiti writers, sticker artists and muralists paint live, or come to the monthly Return to Sender drawing meetup. Artists can contact the group about future exhibitions.

schedule.text: A Return to Sender drawing meetup is held monthly. The site does not list its day, time or place.

cost.text: The site lists no entry cost. It sells a magazine subscription and takes donations.

first_step.how: Email info@unitedstreetart.org to ask for the day and place of the next Return to Sender drawing meetup.
first_step.basis: The site says the public can watch artists at STEP OUTSIDE exhibitions. It names the monthly meetup but gives no day, place or way to join, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: At a STEP OUTSIDE exhibition, the public can watch artists work on walls, panels and doors, and can engage with and learn from them, according to the site. The site does not list exhibition dates, a venue or how long an event runs, so ask before you go. The monthly Return to Sender meetup is for drawing, and the site does not say what to bring or how long it runs.
first_visit_tips: Email info@unitedstreetart.org for the day and place of the next Return to Sender meetup, since the site does not list them.
The address on file is an IRS mailing address, so it may not be where events happen.
The site lists the social accounts @stepoutsideshow and @pmslaps.

records.notes: The group's site is a Google Sites page that unitedstreetart.org redirects to. It names a monthly Return to Sender meetup but gives no day, time, place or sign-up step. Tier 1 called the meetup an open public event, which the site does not say, so newcomer friendliness moved from 3 to 2. No dated events appear on the site, so status stays probably_active with no last sign of life. The About page gives the 2022 formation year and a group phone number, now recorded. The address on file is the IRS mailing address and is kept as published.

records.name: Wynnefield Community Neighborhood Association
records.summary: Wynnefield Community Neighborhood Association is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the West Park part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say. The group is also a nonprofit that runs community events, voter education and youth programs.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors review nearby building and zoning proposals and share the group's view with the City and developers. The group also runs community events, fundraisers, youth programs and voter education, and its home page points to volunteer and team roles.

schedule.text: The site calls its community meeting bi-monthly and holds it on Zoom. It does not give the day or time.

first_step.how: Fill in the online membership application linked from the group's home page, then ask for the Zoom link to the next community meeting.
first_step.basis: The site lists a public zoning meeting on Zoom and an online membership form, and says new members get a free t-shirt. It does not say newcomers are specially welcomed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The zoning meetings are held on Zoom, so you can attend from home. Expect neighbors to talk over nearby building and zoning proposals and to share the group's view with the City and developers. The site does not give a meeting length and does not list any dues.
first_visit_tips: Ask the group for the Zoom link, because the site does not list one.
For meeting details or membership, call 215-600-8701 or email wcnarcoinfo@gmail.com, as the site advises.
In-person special events are held at Mingle Event Studio, 1905 N. 54th Street.

records.notes: Own website found and read. It lists a Zoning RCO public meeting on Zoom on Monday, September 14, 2026, which sets last_sign_of_life to 2026-09. The site gives no meeting day, time or Zoom link and does not list dues. Guessed sub-pages for joining the team, the board and updates returned 404, so they were not read. The site gives 215-598-2410 for its Neighborhood Preservation Committee; the City list number is kept. The About page says the group began in April 2021. Fetches used: 6.

records.name: 100 Black Men of Philadelphia
records.summary: A mentoring nonprofit for young people in Philadelphia. It pairs boys in grades 2 to 12 with mentors, runs leadership and financial literacy programs, and offers a college prep group for students heading to Lincoln or Cheyney University.
records.what_you_do: Youth sign up through the Mentee (Youth) Participation Request form on the site and pick a program, such as the Saturday Leadership Academy. The group also runs financial literacy classes for grades 7 to 12 and workshops on professional skills, resumes and interviews. Men who are 25 or older and live in Philadelphia can apply for membership. Members volunteer at least 40 hours a year, through mentoring, committees or other work, and pay yearly dues.

schedule.text: The Leadership Academy and the online Mentorship Program meet on the 1st and 3rd Saturday of each month. The site does not give the meeting time.

cost.text: The site does not state a fee for the youth programs. Adult members pay yearly dues of $300, and the page lists $350 for some members under 30 or over 60, with unclear wording.

first_step.how: Fill in the Mentee (Youth) Participation Request form on the site and pick the Saturday Leadership Academy.
first_step.basis: A public form on the site lists each program to choose from, so the youth way in is clear. The site does not say how a non-member adult can mentor.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Leadership Academy is for young men in grades 2 to 12, grouped by age and led by mentors. Topics include character, conflict resolution, goal setting and leadership. The site does not give the place, the length or the fee for sessions.
first_visit_tips: Have a parent or guardian's name, phone number, email, school and grade ready, since the form asks for them.
Ask the office for the place and start time, because the site does not list them.
To ask about adult volunteering, call (267) 424-2444 or email office@100blackmenphilly.org.

records.notes: Two enrollment paths are named. The home page has a Click To Enroll button that goes to an Eventbrite page, which is a lead platform and was not read, while the programs page names the Mentee (Youth) Participation Request form. The first step uses the form. The site describes the Leadership Academy as for young men and the Mentorship Program as for boys, and does not say whether girls can take part. The programs page says there is a monthly calendar, but none was on the pages read. The footer copyright year is not treated as evidence. Adult membership: men 25 or older who live in Philadelphia, of good character, sponsored by a current member and approved by the Membership Committee and Board. The page wording on the $350 rate is unclear. Emerging 100 and Collegiate 100 are listed without dates or fees. Fetches used: 4.

records.name: 1812 Productions
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater company that makes comedy and comic theater about community, history, and people. Besides its shows, it runs training programs and holds auditions.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a show or a season subscription, or use a ticket discount. Auditions are held for productions when they are scheduled; none were listed when we checked. 1812 Education brings weekly theater workshops into two Philadelphia public schools. The apprenticeship is a paid full-time job, and its listed application deadline, April 13, 2026, has passed.

schedule.text: Productions run in a yearly season at Plays & Players Theatre. The site does not give a weekly schedule, and show dates are on each show's own page.

cost.text: Tickets and season subscriptions are sold on the site, and ticket discounts are listed. Prices were not on the pages read.

access.notes: A ramp from the sidewalk reaches the lobby. Orchestra rows B to G have no steps, rows H to M have one step, row N has two and row O has three. The mezzanine and lower level are reached only by stairs. Wheelchair and companion seats are booked by phone or email, not online. Some shows are open captioned, and free listening headsets are at the box office. The lower level restrooms are not accessible. The site does not list ASL or sensory-friendly shows.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to one show on the site, then go to Plays & Players Theatre at 1714 Delancey Place.
first_step.basis: Anyone can buy a show ticket on the site, and the box office takes questions by phone and email. No audition was scheduled when we checked, so the ticket is the clearest way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shows at Plays & Players Theatre are seated comedy performances about community, history and people. The orchestra level has the most step-free rows, so ask for seats there if you need them. Tickets are paid, and prices were not on the pages read.
first_visit_tips: Check each show's own page for its dates and prices, since the season list shows no dates.
Wheelchair and companion seats are not sold online, so call 215-592-9560 or email info@1812productions.org to book them.
Free listening headsets are picked up at the box office window, first come, first served, with no reservation.
The lower level restrooms are not wheelchair accessible.

records.notes: The apprenticeship page both says applications are closed and says the company is accepting applications, with an April 13, 2026 deadline. Confirm with the office before anyone applies. The auditions page lists no scheduled auditions. The last sign of life (2026-04) is the apprenticeship deadline printed on the page, not a post date. The Where to Park and Where to Find Us pages were not read, so parking and transit are not recorded. The Vaudevillian Society is a donor recognition program with a $1,812 minimum gift, not a community group, so it was not recorded. The 1812 Education program works through two partner schools and has no public way in. Fetches used: 6.

records.name: AMC Delaware Valley 20s and 30s Group
aka: 20s and 30s Appalachian Mountain Club, Delaware Valley
records.summary: The young adult group of the Appalachian Mountain Club's Delaware Valley chapter, for people in their 20s and 30s. It runs hikes, bike rides, paddling and social outings, and you do not need an AMC membership to take part.
records.what_you_do: Find a 20s/30s outing in the AMC activities database, filtered for the Delaware Valley chapter, then register and go. Outings include hikes, bike rides, paddling, trail work, backpacking and indoor climbing, plus social outings such as picnics and brewery stops. You can also join the group's mailing list by email.

schedule.text: Events run most weekends. Start points and times are not named on the group page, so read each outing listing.

locations.label: Outings in eastern Pennsylvania and north-central New Jersey

cost.text: The group page says most activities are free, and AMC membership is optional. Some other chapter courses and trips charge fees.

first_step.how: Find an outing in the AMC activities database, filtered for the 20s and 30s group in the Delaware Valley chapter, and register for it.
first_step.basis: The group page says most activities are free and open to all, and that registration is the listed step. It does not say beginners are specially welcome or what to bring.
first_step.what_to_expect: Outings cover hikes, bike rides, paddling, trail work, backpacking and social events such as picnics and brewery stops. Most activities are free, and you do not need to be an AMC member. The page does not say how long an outing lasts, where it starts or what to bring.
first_visit_tips: Open each outing listing to find its start point and time, since the group page does not name them.
You do not need an AMC membership to join in.
Join the group's mailing list by email to hear about new outings.

records.notes: The group page has no dated events, and the chapter news archive has no 20s/30s outing dates, so status stays probably_active with no last sign of life. The chapter's email button hides the address, so no email is recorded. The 'events run most weekends' line is carried from tier 1; the pages read in this pass do not confirm it. The page does not name Philadelphia for these outings. The group stays in because it belongs to the Delaware Valley chapter and its page covers eastern Pennsylvania, which includes Philadelphia. The chapter news archive shows a 2026 bike challenge that requires AMC membership, and some trips and courses with fees. These belong to the chapter, not this group, so they were not recorded. Fetches used: 4 for this group.

notes: Seven groups in the batch, seven records written (publish 7, hide 0, other verdicts 0). WebFetch used 26 times, all within the per group limit; WebSearch used 1 of 1 (it found no website or schedule for the two Wynnefield groups that have only Facebook pages). No 403, bot check or rate limiting was seen. Several guessed sub-page URLs returned 404 and are noted in each record; the 1812 auditions page redirected to its auditions-2 page. Facebook and Eventbrite pages were not read for facts. Leads checked and dropped with reasons: Vaudevillian Society (a donor recognition program of 1812 Productions, not a community group) and AMC-DV Lehigh Valley Group (meets in Bethlehem, does not mention Philadelphia; out of area, not recorded). American Theatre Wing is named as a partner on the 1812 site but is a national organization, so it was not added as a lead. Owner decisions to check: (1) Wynnefield Heights and Wynnefield Residents keep tier 1 status active, based only on the City RCO list; (2) the AMC 20s and 30s group is kept although its page names eastern Pennsylvania rather than Philadelphia; (3) the 100 Black Men site describes its youth programs as for young men and boys, and does not say whether girls can take part; (4) the 1812 apprenticeship page contradicts itself about whether applications are open.
